cards.title: One append-only run ledger for bench and follow-through; bench.json becomes a view

cards.body:
## Summary
A playbook's runs live in a 12-line rolling window inside bench.json, and follow-through keeps its runs in a different, append-only file with its own correction rule. Make one module, `ledger.py`, the only writer of run records for both: append-only lines and corrections in `playbooks/<id>/bench.runs.json` (and follow-through's existing file), newest correction wins, pooled by key. bench.json stays as the desktop reads it, a derived view of the latest run plus the last HISTORY lines and a `pool` block.

## Description
The ranking (ADR 0128) pools every comparable run, but the pool is whatever survives `history[-HISTORY:]`. One playbook already holds 11 history lines, and 20 have n >= 3; `bench --runs k`, which ADR 0128 asks for, fills the window fast, and a rescore's correction takes a line and pushes a real run out. The audit-logging standard's append-only-design technique says a record is never dropped to make room and a correction refers to what it corrects; follow-through already does exactly that (followthrough.py:784-823) with its own copy of read/append/correct/tally. One ledger module removes the duplicate rule, removes the bound, and adds a hash chain so an edited line is caught. Readers fall back to bench.json when no ledger exists, so the committed library and ranking.json do not change until a playbook is benched again; no data migration is in the write set.

## Flow
- ledger.append(root, filename, line) / ledger.correct(root, filename, mark, was, now) / ledger.pool(root, key) / ledger.verify(root, filename)
- write_bench appends the run's headline to bench.runs.json, then derives bench.json's history and `pool` from the ledger
- rescore appends a correction, never a history line
- rank.runs_of and evidence._runs read ledger.pool (fallback: bench.json)
- followthrough's record_run/record_correction/tally call the ledger, file format unchanged

## Expected impact
The ranking and the narration stand on every run benched under the key, however many; a rescore never costs a run; two run-record implementations become one; an edited history line is detectable. The desktop's own comparableRuns (another context) can later read the `pool` block instead of recomputing.

## Evaluation
Claim: the pool is unbounded and corrections cost nothing, with today's outputs unchanged where no ledger exists.
Before: 0 of 4 new-behaviour acceptance cases pass (cases 0, 1, 6, 7); guards 2-5 green
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases, offline with the existing scripted_model world factory, plus `rank --check`
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: Every missed item says whether she saw it: seen-and-passed vs never surfaced
acceptance: a scripted run that reads the page holding eligible item K and files no card for K -> report['attribution']['missed'] has K with seen: true, read_by: ['host.<app>.<tool>'] and the CLI prints 'missed K - seen on <tool>, not filed'
a scripted run that never pages past page 1 when K is on page 2 -> K is seen: false and the CLI prints 'missed K - never surfaced (page 2 of 2 of <tool> not read)'
a filed trap T -> attribution.traps lists T with the read that showed it, so a trap is told apart from an unfounded guess

rescore of a saved report.json written before this change (transcript calls carry name+params, no outputs) -> attribution is rebuilt by replaying each recorded READ through SimulatedPortals and equals the live run's attribution for the same cards
attribution never reads truth inside the page: SimulatedPortals has no access to truth.json and its answers are byte-identical with attribution on or off
score() output, SCORER_VERSION, verdict reasons and the comparability key are unchanged for the same cards -> rank --check stays green and evidence --verify reports no narration drift
summary_of(report) carries `attribution` {missed_seen, missed_unseen, by_item} into bench.json; headline() and history lines are unchanged

cards.body:
## Summary
After a short run the operator reads 'found 4 of 9 items' and has to open a 4,000-character-per-turn transcript to learn whether Athena never saw the other five (a world, page or pagination problem: fix the playbook) or saw them and walked past (a judgement problem: fix the prompt or accept the model). The bench already has everything to say which, per item; it just never joins the reads to the truth.

## Description
A new pure module `attribution.py` takes the playbook and a report: it replays every READ call the transcript recorded through SimulatedPortals (pure over world.json, page.py:118), collects the rows she was shown, and for every missed eligible item and every filed trap says seen or never surfaced, which read showed it, and for an unseen paged item which page was never read. It runs after score() in run_bench and rescore, outside the page (which must not know the truth, page.py:12), and outside score() so SCORER_VERSION and every comparability key stay put. The CLI prints one line per missed item; bench.json carries the counts and per-item rows so the desktop's run view can show them later. Technique: eval-harness failure-signatures-beside-the-pass-rate (count each failing item by the family of failure beside the recall) feeding failure-attribution (it makes the manual sample choosable).

## Flow
- run_bench / rescore -> score(cards) unchanged -> attribute(playbook, report) -> report['attribution']
- __main__.bench prints 'missed K - seen on X, not filed' or 'missed K - never surfaced (page p of n of X not read)'
- summary_of keeps attribution in bench.json; headline/history untouched

## Expected impact
Every short run names its failure family per item on the line the operator already reads: the resale-certificate playbook's 'the order list could not be paged' diagnosis that docs/features/playbooks.md:163 records as found by hand becomes the bench's own output, and rescore after a world fix shows the item flip from unseen to found.

## Evaluation
Claim: a missed item's failure family is printed and recorded, with score, verdict and keys unchanged.
Before: 0 of 5 new-behaviour cases pass (0, 1, 2, 3, 6); guards 4-5 green
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases with the existing scripted_model world factory, offline
Result: better
Gate: none
